input.subject: Incorrect checksum in control file with pg_rewind test

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the bug or either fix. The race is reproduced in message #3, and both designs reuse existing mechanisms. The one open point is prior-attempts-1: message #5 names another thread with its own fix and CommitFest entry, and nobody has said which patch is the candidate. That is a coordination question to settle before commit, not a flaw in the idea.

brief.title: Fix torn reads of pg_control in EXEC_BACKEND child processes
brief.problem: In builds with EXEC_BACKEND, child processes read pg_control from disk without ControlFileLock. A child can read a partly written file while the startup process updates it during WAL replay, and then fails with "incorrect checksum in control file". The failure is rare and was seen in TAP tests on the author's local CI.
brief.proposed_design: The v1 patch retries the pg_control read on a CRC failure, as commit 5725e4ebe7a9 did for frontend programs. Korotkov proposed instead that the postmaster pass its copy of the control file to the child through BackendParameters, as fork builds already inherit it. The author accepted that alternative.
author_claims: The race affects only EXEC_BACKEND builds, because LocalProcessControlFile cannot take ControlFileLock.
The failure is not specific to pg_rewind and can happen at any time.
A dirty test hack plus a pg_update_control_file() loop and pgbench reproduces it on master.
Korotkov claims passing the control file through BackendParameters stops torn reads and removes a difference between fork and EXEC_BACKEND.
v1 copies the frontend fix with little change.
brief.thread_state: Kovmir confirmed the repro, Korotkov posted an alternative patch, and the author approved it. Lakhin pointed to another thread with its own fix and CommitFest entry, and nobody said how the two relate; CFbot reports the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: Which patch the CommitFest entry now tracks, v1 or Korotkov's BackendParameters patch.
How this entry relates to the fix and CommitFest entry in the thread Lakhin linked.
Whether the fix should be back-patched, and to which branches.
Whether any setup other than EXEC_BACKEND builds, such as Windows, hits the race in practice.
Whether children may need a newer pg_control than the postmaster's copy when they start.

objections.failure_scenario: Two CommitFest entries carry different fixes for the same EXEC_BACKEND torn read. A committer reviews this entry while the other fix is being reviewed or committed elsewhere. Reviewer time is split, and the second fix to land either conflicts with the first or duplicates its work.

No later message says how the two fixes compare or which one should go forward. Message #6 approves Korotkov's BackendParameters patch, but the entry still names only the v1 author and needs a rebase. A committer would likely ask which patch, in which entry, is the candidate.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fixes for non-atomic read of read of control file on ext4 + ntfs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Fix torn reads of pg_control on ext4 and NTFS, where a concurrent write can make a reader see mixed old and new contents and fail the CRC check. The patch set added a retry loop in frontend programs, ControlFileLock in SQL functions and base backup, and, while a backup runs, a write of a new control file that durable_rename() puts in place.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Thomas Munro committed the frontend retry loop and the missing locks in the SQL functions, so only the backup patches were left in the entry. Robert Haas asked for comments and a clearer commit message on 0002 and a cleaner refactoring of update_controlfile() in 0001. A proposal to put the control file in backup_label was also still under debate. The author did not post a new version, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I have changed the status of this to "Waiting on Author" as Robert's comments have not yet been handled.

precedents_retrieved.title: Configurable location for extension .control files
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started with a request to make the directory that holds extension .control files configurable, so isolated package layouts such as NixOS can install extensions outside SHAREDIR/extension. A 2015 patch added an extension_directory setting that superusers can change at runtime, mainly so extension authors can test their .control files in a local cluster.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected in 2013 that the path should not be adjustable at runtime because of security concerns. In review, Heikki Linnakangas said tests also need dynamic_library_path changed, and other share data such as timezone and tsearch files is not covered. He proposed that pgxs build a temporary installation so "make check" works for extensions, and the entry was returned with feedback in that direction.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In summary, the goal is to make "make check" to work for extensions, and the way to do that is to teach pgxs to create a temporary installation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix PGXS so built control files work with VPATH builds
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pgxs.mk so that the $(EXTENSION).control file is found along the VPATH instead of only in $(srcdir). Extensions that generate their control file could then do VPATH builds from a read-only source tree.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut offered a simpler patch using vpathsearch, which Craig Ringer rejected because it depends on the VPATH variable rather than vpath directives. No one answered Craig's follow-up. The CFBot then reported failures in the test_extensions and test_extdepend suites, and with no new version the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
With the thread stalled and the tests still failing, I've marked this patch
Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: add the last checkpoint kind to the control file
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Julien Rouhaud, Kyotaro Horiguchi, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: Store the flags of the last completed checkpoint (shutdown, end-of-recovery, immediate, force and so on) in the control file. Show them through pg_control_checkpoint() and pg_controldata, so users can see the checkpoint kind without reading the server logs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers saw no realistic use for the kind of an already completed checkpoint and preferred a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view for the checkpoint in progress. The control file must stay within 512 bytes, so its space is kept for critical data, and two bytes for non-critical data were judged a likely future regret. The stored flags also leave out flags added when a running checkpoint is upgraded, for example by a later CHECKPOINT command. The author agreed to drop the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For now we have some room, but we will likely keep consuming bytes in that file
for more critical features and it's almost certain that at one point we will
regret wasting 2 bytes for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT state for control file
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops the end-of-recovery checkpoint from setting the control file state to DB_SHUTDOWNING and then DB_SHUTDOWNED, which the author considered wrong. Two variants were posted: one adds a new state DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT, and one keeps DB_IN_CRASH_RECOVERY or DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY until DB_IN_PRODUCTION.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier argued that the current state is not incorrect, because an end-of-recovery checkpoint is a shutdown checkpoint and the code has relied on that for about 10 years. He said the change was not checked against other assumptions, such as unlogged relation reset needing a clean shutdown, and that it leaves an invalid minimum recovery point in DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY. He added that it would make back-patching harder in a sensitive area, and the entry was closed after the thread went quiet.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This
patch would bring some extra visibility for something that's not
incorrect either on HEAD, as end-of-recovery checkpoints are the same
things as shutdown checkpoints.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add recovery to pg_control and remove backup_label
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Andres Freund, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes backup_label and stores the recovery information in pg_control instead. pg_backup_stop() returns an updated pg_control as bytea for the backup software to store, which also avoids copying a torn pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to changing the backup API again and asked for more senior votes before a change this large. Andres Freund (his view is visible only in quoted replies) stayed on the fence, saying it helps pg_basebackup but not external backups and removes a human-readable file used for debugging. Once incremental backup was committed and depended on backup_label, Michael Paquier proposed returning the entry, and the author withdrew it rather than rework the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It would be a lot of work with all the new changes for incremental backup and since Andres and Robert appear to be very against the idea, I doubt it would be worth the effort.

precedents_retrieved.title: logical replication access control
precedents_retrieved.summary: A patch set to let ordinary users with explicit privileges manage logical replication instead of requiring superuser or replication roles. It added a PUBLICATION privilege on tables, a USAGE privilege on publications, a CREATE SUBSCRIPTION privilege on databases, privilege checks in apply workers, and normal database entries in pg_hba.conf for logical replication.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Stephen Frost argued that publishing a table should be an owner right rather than a grantable privilege, and the author dropped the PUBLICATION privilege in favor of owner rights. The author withdrew the USAGE privilege on publications because of issues raised in the thread. The author then returned the rest because a CREATE SUBSCRIPTION privilege granted on a database could be assigned by a database owner who may not be privileged enough to make that decision. Two parts were committed: the publication owner fix and the pg_hba.conf change.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
One new concern I just thought about is that having GRANT whatever ON
DATABASE would allow a database owner to assign these privileges, but a
database owner is not necessarily someone highly privileged to make this
decision.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add a GUC variable that control logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a session-level GUC, logical_replication (default true), that sets a new xinfo flag on commit when turned off. Logical decoding then skips the flagged transaction as if it had aborted, so bulk deletes in one session are not replicated.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that skipping changes is a decision for each decoding plugin, so one user-settable GUC would also hide changes from plugins such as an audit log; he called it the wrong approach and pointed to ALTER PUBLICATION, separate publications, or new hooks. Craig Ringer noted that the DoNotReplicateId replication origin already suppresses replication of a transaction and asked that any such feature be superuser-only. Michael Paquier marked it Returned with feedback for lack of support.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In any case, this kind of thing needs to be handled by the decoding
plugin based on its configuration policies and depending on its needs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
Reverted commit(s): Read extension script files in text not binary mode.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert commit 924e03917 in favor of adding code to convert \r\n to \n
explicitly, on Windows only.  The idea of letting text mode do the
work fails for a couple of reasons:

* Per Microsoft documentation, text mode also causes control-Z to be
interpreted as end-of-file.  While it may be unlikely that extension
scripts contain control-Z, we've historically allowed it, and breaking
the case doesn't seem wise.

* Apparently, on some Windows configurations, "r" mode is interpreted
as binary not text mode.  We could force it with "rt" but that would
be inconsistent with our code elsewhere, and it would still require
Windows-specific coding.

Thanks to Alexander Lakhin for investigation.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent rejected this idea. P1's committed frontend retry is the model for v1, and P6 is about backup_label and does not apply. The only concern from this angle is the duplicate fix reported in message #5.

The proposal has no user-facing contract: no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, pg_dump output or psql change, and no client-visible behaviour beyond removing a spurious FATAL. Both designs (CRC retry, or passing pg_control through BackendParameters) change only internal EXEC_BACKEND startup, and BackendParameters is private to the server binary. Back-patching therefore raises no ABI concern from this angle. The unresolved overlap with the other thread and CommitFest entry is a process question for other angles.

Neither patch changes the on-disk format of pg_control, the WAL, the catalogs, the wire protocol or any extension-facing struct. BackendParameters passes only between a postmaster and children of the same binary, and children get the same snapshot fork builds already inherit, so I see no replication or pg_upgrade failure scenario.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes how EXEC_BACKEND child processes get their copy of pg_control, either by retrying the read or by inheriting the postmaster's copy through BackendParameters. It adds no SQL surface, privilege, role or setting, and exposes no new data to any user. A child already reads the whole control file today, so it learns nothing new. The BackendParameters file is created by the postmaster for the server's own children with the server's existing file permissions. No security objection applies.

No maintenance or fit objection holds. The BackendParameters patch from message #4 makes EXEC_BACKEND children inherit the same pg_control snapshot that fork children already get, so it removes a divergence and adds no per-query cost, no new API and no new dependency. What remains open is not a design flaw: which patch the entry tracks, how it relates to the fix Lakhin linked in message #5, and the back-patch scope.

This is a bugfix. Both designs reuse existing mechanisms: the frontend retry loop and BackendParameters. No extension or existing setting can prevent the torn read, so the only concern from this angle is the duplicate fix in another thread.

This entry fixes a real bug: child processes in EXEC_BACKEND builds fail with "incorrect checksum in control file". Kovmir reproduced it independently (message #3), Lakhin points to a second thread about the same issue (message #5), and the frontend version of the race was already fixed ([P1]), so demand is not in doubt. Windows builds always start children with exec, so real users are exposed, and the cost falls only on the EXEC_BACKEND startup path.
